title: Bharata: Governing in Rama's Name
subtitle: The sandals become a sign of delegated rule

learningObjectives.text: What does Bharata do with the throne?

sandals.author: Valmiki
sandals.locator: Ayodhyakandam · Section CXII; Ayodhyakandam · Section CXII, normalized characters 3098-3503
sandals.excerpt: Thereupon taking off his sandals, that highly energetic one gave them to the magnanimous Bharata. Bharata, bowing down unto the sandals, said, "O hero, for four and ten years shall I, wearing matted locks and bark, and subsisting upon fruits and roots, O scion of the Raghu race, expecting thy arrival, remain outside the city, having, O subduer of foes, made over the task of government unto thy sandals.
sandals.note: Verbatim English translation from Dutt. The Mahabharata volume is a condensed verse rendering; the Ramayana volume contains only the Balakandam and Ayodhyakandam.

narrativeBlocks.title: A crown he never wanted
narrativeBlocks.body: Bharata returns to Ayodhya to find his father dead and his mother Kaikeyi has exiled Rama and made him king — a gift procured by treachery that he never asked for.

narrativeBlocks.title: The brother who begs
narrativeBlocks.body: He marches to the forest — not with an army but an entreaty: come back, take the crown, it was stolen in my name. Rama refuses: the exile-term is his father's word, and a word stands.

narrativeBlocks.title: The sandals on the throne
narrativeBlocks.body: Bharata's compromise is one of the epic's most beautiful gestures: he takes Rama's sandals, sets them on the throne, and rules from a hut outside the city — regent in name only, his brother's footwear as king.

narrativeBlocks.title: Fourteen years of waiting
narrativeBlocks.body: For the whole exile he governs in Rama's name, in mourning garb, awaiting the return — loyalty as a fourteen-year vigil.

narrativeBlocks.title: The other ideal
narrativeBlocks.body: Rama embodies obedience; Bharata embodies loyalty without ambition — the brother who could have taken everything and chose the sandals instead.

quiz.prompt: What do Rama's sandals on the throne mean?

quiz.explanation: The sandals are the throne's occupant for fourteen years.
